title: The roommate's midnight deliveries
hook: My roommate kept receiving food deliveries neither of us had ordered.
story: It happened every night at exactly 11:11. At first we blamed an app glitch. Then I answered the door and found a tiny paper bag with a receipt inside. The only message was, 'Stop pretending you live alone.' I showed it to my roommate. He stared at it before asking, 'Did the driver see you?'
ending: Then he admitted he'd been paying for a second person's meals for months. He just wouldn't tell me who.

title: The group chat betrayal
hook: I found out my friends had a group chat without me.
story: I wasn't upset at first. People have different chats. Then one friend sent me a screenshot meant for that group. It was a poll asking who should tell me I wasn't invited to the weekend trip. Three people voted to lie. One person voted to tell me. I asked why they hadn't said anything sooner.
ending: They replied, 'Because I thought you already knew. You were the one who cancelled the trip.' I had never cancelled anything.

title: The interview that went backwards
hook: My job interview ended with the interviewer asking me for a favour.
story: The first ten minutes were normal: experience, teamwork, deadlines. Then the interviewer asked about a small tool I'd built for fun. His team had been trying to solve the exact same problem for weeks. I explained how it worked, assuming it was a test.
ending: He closed his laptop and said, 'Forget the interview. Would you be willing to teach our team how you did that?'

title: The mystery birthday present
hook: Every year, someone leaves my neighbour the same birthday present.
story: A plain envelope appears on his doorstep on the same date. No name, no return address. Last year he opened it in front of me. Inside was a photograph of him as a child beside a person he said he had never met. On the back was one sentence: 'You promised you'd remember.'
ending: It was the date his childhood best friend moved away, and the promise they'd made before saying goodbye.

title: The office fridge rule
hook: Someone at work kept putting warning labels on my lunch.
story: The first note said, 'Don't eat this.' I assumed it was a joke. The next day, another note appeared: 'Seriously, leave it alone.' I asked the office group chat who was doing it. Nobody answered. At lunch, the manager took my container and put it in a locked cabinet.
ending: The fridge was being replaced, and my lunch was the surprise cake for my promotion. Everyone had been told not to touch it.

title: The number saved as DON'T ANSWER
hook: My phone showed a missed call from a contact I never saved.
story: The contact name was 'DON'T ANSWER'. I checked my contacts and it wasn't there. A minute later, the number called again. I ignored it and got a text: 'You still have my keys.' I remembered the spare key I'd found in an old jacket pocket. I replied asking who it was.
ending: It was my old landlord. I'd moved out two years ago, and somehow the key had travelled with me.

title: The neighbour's apartment guide
hook: My new neighbour knew things about my apartment before I moved in.
story: He warned me which cupboard door stuck, which window rattled in the wind, and which light switch needed two presses. Then he mentioned exactly where the previous tenant had hidden a spare key. I asked how he knew. He admitted he'd helped the previous tenant move out.

title: The package on the wrong doorstep
hook: A parcel arrived at my flat with my name on it, but I hadn't ordered anything.

ending: My mum finally admitted she'd found it in an old family photo album and sent it because it was the last thing my late grandad had bought me.

hook: My cousin changed the wedding seating chart and put me beside someone I hadn't spoken to in years.
story: I assumed it was a mistake until I saw the name clearly printed beside mine. At the reception, the person sat down and immediately apologised for an argument we'd had at school. I hadn't even remembered it. Then they slid a small envelope across the table.

title: The mystery playlist
hook: A stranger kept adding songs to a playlist I had made years ago.

title: The lift button
hook: Someone in my apartment building kept pressing my floor before getting into the lift.
story: It happened three evenings in a row. I'd enter the lift, and the button for my floor was already lit. I asked the caretaker if the lift was faulty. He checked the service log and found nothing. On the fourth evening, I waited in the lobby instead of going straight up.

title: The wrong group project

title: The forgotten birthday

title: The empty shop
hook: A tiny shop near my house looked closed for months, but every morning its sign changed.
story: One day it said 'Back soon'. The next it said 'Not today'. Then it displayed a different handwritten message every morning. I finally knocked on the door and an older man answered. He said he wasn't running a shop anymore; he was practising lettering for his granddaughter's art exam.

title: The borrowed book
hook: I bought a second-hand book and found a letter addressed to someone with my exact name.
story: The letter was folded between two chapters and dated twenty years earlier. It described a small family disagreement and ended with an apology. I checked the return address, but the house had been demolished. I took the letter to the bookshop, hoping they might know the previous owner.
ending: The shopkeeper recognised the handwriting: it was his own. He'd written it to his brother and never posted it. He asked if he could finally send a photo of it.
